stem:
Ajay's science walk near a reserve forest outside Dehradun shows dense herbs, shrubs and trees with birds, insects and deer.

Why is this forest more than just a group of trees?

options.text: A few scattered plants can count as a forest whenever they give animals some food.
Forests grow dense plants because animals first decide they need food and shelter there.
Dense, varied plant growth provides food and shelter, so many animals, birds and insects can live there together.
A green lawn next to the school gate is the same kind of forest home because it is green.

teacher.key_rationale: A forest is a dense, varied plant community that shelters many life forms. A drops the dense-growth condition; B reverses cause and effect; D captures green colour alone.
